_comment: Anansi ghost-text whispers shown during stage exploration travel. Wry, knowing, never tactical. One line each, no names, no mechanical terms.
travel: The land remembers feet it hasn't felt in years.
Walk slow. The ground is still deciding what it thinks of you.
Every stolen story leaves a groove in the dirt.
I've seen quicker travelers. I've seen wiser ones too.
Patience, patience. Even a web is built one thread at a time.
Something here was named once. It misses that.
The dust holds shapes longer than memory does.
You're not lost. You're just early to where you're going.
A story wants to be found more than it wants to be safe.
I spun through here once. Left a little of myself behind.
The wind carries names it was never given permission to keep.
Careful — even silence around here used to be a voice.
Some ground was walked so often it forgot it was ground.
I like watching feet decide things minds haven't caught up to yet.
This place was stolen gently, which is the worst way.
Keep walking. Even I don't know what's listening back.
A thread pulled taut enough hums if you're patient.
Not every step needs a reason. Some just need feet.
The land keeps its grudges longer than its gratitude.
Somewhere near here, a story is still waiting to be asked its name.
I do enjoy watching someone else do the wandering for once.
Even lost things prefer to be lost together.
There's a hush here that used to be a song.
Don't mind me. I'm only weaving what you're walking.
